All the five Petitioners are present in the Court Hall.
The learned advocate for these Petitioners identifies each of them in the open Court.
Vakilpatra on behalf of Respondent No.2 ( four pages) is taken on record and marked as 'X-1' for identification.
2. The Original Complainant, Respondent No.2 is present 905-wp5059-21.odt in the Court hall.
His learned Advocate identifies him in the open Court.
3. The Original Petitioner, Pushpak and Respondent No.2, the Complainant, had tendered the consent terms dated 5 th September, 2020 in this Court, from pages 19 to 21.
However, it was only Pushpak and his lawyer who have signed the consent terms document.
Hence, this consent terms are ignored.
4. Today, the Complainant, who is Respondent No.2 herein, tenders an affidavit dated 24th July, 2025 (four pages) which is taken on record and marked as 'X-2' for identification.

5. The offence registered by virtue of FIR No.43 of 2020 registered on 25th January,
2020 with L.T. Marg Police Station, Mumbai, was under Sections 409, 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
All parties conceded that a heinous crime was not committed.
A commercial transaction led to the lodging of an FIR.
All pray that the FIR be quashed by consent of the parties.
6. The learned APP submits that considering the type of 905-wp5059-21.odt offence urged, it is left to the Court to pass an appropriate order.

7. All parties have vouched that the matter has been settled between the parties and there would be no request by any of them, any time in future, for seeking restoration of this Petition or for restoration of the FIR.
A charge-sheet has also been filed.
However, the charge is not framed, is the contention of the parties.
8. In view of the above, this Petition is allowed in terms of prayer clause (b) in the light of the affidavit marked 'X-2' and the statements of these parties that they have resolved this issue.

9. Needless to state that Case CC No.419/PW/2022 before 3rd Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, at Esplanade Court would stand disposed off and the parties would appear before the concerned Court along with a copy of this order obtained from the official website of the Bombay High Court, for passing a formal order of disposing off the matter.
